Pressure Technologies PLC Reports Steady Trade Figures for First Half of the Year

Sheffield-based Pressure Technologies PLC, a key player in the UK’s Machinery sector, has released its routine trade figures for the first half of 2024, indicating stable performance across its core segments. The company, which specialises in the design and manufacture of high-pressure systems, reported revenues broadly in line with expectations, reflecting steady demand from energy, defence, and industrial clients.

According to the company’s interim statement, group revenues reached £18.6 million for the six-month period ending March 31, compared to £18.2 million for the same period last year. Gross margin remained consistent at 25.1%, while order intake showed a modest increase, with management attributing the rise to a gradual uptick in infrastructure investment across the UK.

John Redfern, CEO of Pressure Technologies PLC, commented, “Our order book continues to reflect healthy demand from our long-term customers, particularly in the energy and defence sectors. We are encouraged by the resilience of our operations, and our priority remains delivering quality and reliability.”

Industry analysts welcomed the figures, noting the company’s ability to maintain stable performance despite a competitive market. “Pressure Technologies’ results demonstrate operational discipline and healthy customer relationships,” said Lydia Morris, an analyst at Northgate Finance Consultants.

The British Machinery Manufacturers’ Association also noted the positive trend. “The figures from Pressure Technologies are a strong indicator of the sector’s ongoing stability,” said spokesperson Simon Patel.

Pressure Technologies PLC employs over 200 people in the South Yorkshire region and continues to invest in workforce training and equipment upgrades. The company stated it expects trading conditions to remain stable in the coming months.
